Authorized staff may import an approved monitoring workbook or add students and subject rows directly in the portal. Every value is labelled with its source (Imported, Manual entry or System); a value entered in the portal carries the name of the person, the time and, where required, a reason, and every change is kept with its previous value. Grades are never entered in the portal. entries.match: Checks each student's required research submissions
entries.replace: Checks each student's required research submissions for the gate the student is currently at: title defense (Form 1), proposal defense readiness, final defense, and completion evidence. The ethics review (Form 5.1 and Form 5.2) forms part of the proposal gate and opens only after the proposal defense is passed. Required documents are defined per gate. The Academic Coordinator endorses Form 1 and the three concept papers with an in-system signature before panel matching opens, and a rule-based concept paper check reports missing sections as advice without blocking the endorsement. The assigned adviser signs the proposal and final manuscripts and endorsements in the system, each signature being tied to the exact uploaded file, so that a replacement file returns to the adviser. The panel chair records the defense result in the faculty portal: passed, passed with minor revisions, provisional pass with re-defense, provisional pass with revisions for panel approval, deferred, or failed (for the title defense, approved or disapproved). Revisions are submitted by the student and confirmed by the adviser or the panel chair before the stage completes.
entries.note: 5.3.5. RESEARCH_MILESTONES (four gates), form1_endorsement_queue/endorse_form1, evaluate_concept_paper_text, ADVISER_APPROVAL_DOCUMENTS, faculty verdict routes, tests/test_research_core.py.

entries.match: Recommends a defense panel by matching
entries.replace: Recommends a defense panel by comparing the body text of the student's current research paper (the concept papers, the proposal manuscript or the final manuscript, depending on the stage) with each faculty member's recorded expertise: the profile specialization and expertise records such as research interests, publications, past advisee and panel titles, and degrees. The research title and file names are excluded. Similarity is computed by TF-IDF cosine similarity, or by Gemini embeddings where a key is configured, with TF-IDF as the fallback. The score combines expertise match (60 points), availability (25, scored from the free windows in the connected Google Calendar or from the availability the faculty member entered; a member who has entered nothing scores zero) and workload (15), and the student's adviser and co-adviser are excluded. The recommendation is advisory: it produces a ranked shortlist with the reason and the matched passage for each suggestion, and a suggested panel seated by role. The coordinator makes the selection, and the server checks it against the panel composition rules of the Graduate School Research Protocol before it is saved.

entries.match: Finds a defense slot at which the student and the panel
entries.replace: Finds a defense slot at which the research adviser and every panel member who has entered availability are simultaneously free. Availability is never assumed: it consists of the weekly working hours and the dated entries (not available, or available only at stated hours) that each faculty member enters in the faculty portal, less the defenses already booked. Where a faculty member has connected a Google Calendar, that member's busy periods are removed as well; only free/busy information is read and nothing is written to the calendar. A faculty member who has entered nothing is shown as not entered and is left out of the overlap, and a booking that includes such a person raises a warning; staff can ask the person to enter availability from the same screen. If a connected calendar cannot be read, no slot is proposed for the panel and the chosen time is refused. Slots are two hours long, between 08:00 and 18:00. Proposed dates begin only after the lead time, 14 days by default and held in the business-rules register: it is counted from the Form 1 endorsement for the title defense, and from the date the panel received the manuscript for the proposal and final defenses. A booking cannot be saved if the time is in the past, a panel member or the adviser is outside the entered hours or has an overlapping defense, the venue is taken, the student has an overlapping defense, or a panel member has declined the invitation. Two warnings can be overridden with a recorded reason: a date before the lead time, and a panel member who has not entered availability. A booked defense can be rescheduled or cancelled with a recorded reason and the name of who asked, and the earlier record is kept. A change of panel, which also needs a reason, puts the booking on hold until staff re-confirm it against the availability of the new panel.
entries.note: 5.3.7 (rewritten after the calendar packet). defense_availability_context, GOOGLE_ASSUMED_HOURS only for a connected member with no hours, book_defense_schedule hard/soft conflicts, reschedule/cancel/reconfirm routes; tests/test_calendar_appointments.py.

entries.match: Applies only to the programs that require practicum.
entries.replace: Applies only to the programs that require practicum (the Psychology programs and the Master of Science in Guidance and Counseling). Tracks memorandum of agreement submission, the practicum site and supervisor, the required hours (200 by default, set in the business rules), the completed hours entered by the student as a running total, and the certificates submitted as evidence. Every certificate submission is kept and counted automatically, so that further certificates from other establishments are added rather than replacing the earlier ones. A shortfall in hours leaves the case at Hours Incomplete, and the Academic Coordinator requests additional certificates or returns the case if the organization is not accepted. Once hours and documents are verified, the Academic Coordinator sends a status report to the Dean, who marks it reviewed. Student submission is locked until the eligibility conditions are met.

entries.match: Determines eligibility from coursework completion, comprehensive examination status
entries.replace: Determines eligibility from coursework completion, completion of each research stage (requirements, panel, confirmed schedule and a passing defense result), the post-defense completion documents, and practicum where applicable; the comprehensive examination is a condition for starting the research stages. Candidates are listed for a review window (a school year), and applications open only when the student is eligible. Candidates are processed in named batches in sequence: Graduate School staff compile the batch, the Academic Coordinator checks coursework, the Research Coordinator validates research and practicum, and staff prepare the endorsement list and send it to the Dean. A candidate found incomplete is listed as not eligible with the missing requirements and may resubmit. The Dean approves the list or returns it to staff for revision, and after approval the Dean exports the endorsed list as a file for manual transmission to the Registrar.

entries.match: Structured applications validated by explicit rules
entries.replace: Leave of absence and readmission run on a single case record. Structured applications are validated by explicit rules rather than by interpretation of an uploaded letter: the allowed reasons, the permitted duration (up to two semesters a request and four in total, with no limit on the number of leaves), and the filing date (no leave in the last two weeks of a semester); a leave can be extended once, right after it. Graduate School staff review the request and forward it to the Dean, who may approve it, return it for revision, or deny it. A student may withdraw a request before the Dean decides, and may cancel an approved leave that has not started. On approval the student's standing, enrollment tag and affected subject enrollments are updated when the leave begins, and the approved case joins a Registrar list that staff export as a CSV or Excel file; the list is handed over manually, and staff record when it was sent and acknowledged. Time on leave counts toward maximum residence, and the residency clock is never paused. Staff work the cases on a staged board with drag and drop, and staff and the Dean can apply a step to several cases at once. A readmission request follows the same path; its approval returns the student to active standing, closes the linked leave, and leaves enrollment planning to the Academic Coordinator.
entries.note: 5.3.10. leave_workflow.py, leave_case/leave_case_event/leave_export_log tables, LeaveCasesBoard.jsx; tests/test_loa_readmission.py.

entries.match: Monitors students who have stopped attending without filing a leave
entries.replace: Monitors students whose record shows absence without an approved leave, and applies the policy review for a return from AWOL. AWOL is created from explicit evidence (a recorded AWOL standing, a full-semester withdrawal with no approved leave, or a leave that ended without a return); in the last case AWOL is only proposed, and staff confirm it. Residency enrollment is recorded, and years in program are derived from the recorded entry year and never reduced by leave. A return from AWOL is decided by the Dean, and a student beyond the absolute maximum residence requires full re-enrollment rather than a simple return. A provisional Registrar sheet can be generated for a Dean-approved return and for an active residency record.

entries.match: The monitoring sheet is the consolidated cohort view that the existing spreadsheet cannot provide.
entries.replace: The monitoring sheet is the consolidated cohort view that the existing spreadsheet cannot provide. Each row is a student and each column group is a curriculum category (Basic, Major, and Cognate) with one column per subject, followed by the comprehensive examination and the research milestones. Cell shading encodes the status vocabulary: completed, taken, enrolled, planned, incomplete, failed, dropped, withdrawn, and not taken, and a marker shows where a value was entered by hand. The screen carries a notice that entries typed in the portal are marked Manual entry with the user's name and the time and are kept in the change history, that a later upload that disagrees with a portal entry is held for review, and that grades are not entered here; for roles that cannot edit, it states that the sheet is view only. Graduate School staff and the Academic Coordinator add students and subject rows and edit statuses directly, and the record panel of a student shows each value's source and history. Students carrying a standing condition are labelled inline, and an integrity banner reports enrollment and profile inconsistencies found by comparing the enrollment ledger with the monitoring rows. The view is filtered by program, semester, progress, risk, and enrollment state, and exports to CSV or as an Excel workbook.

The screen also carries the onboarding report of each import batch and the Dean's decision on it, and it is open to Graduate School staff only.

entries.replace: The research gate screen shows, for the selected student, the four stages (title defense, proposal defense readiness, final defense, and completion) and the requirements of the stage in progress, with which are submitted, which await an adviser signature or staff action, and which are outstanding. The Academic Coordinator endorses Form 1 from a queue on the same screen, and the Research Coordinator records the ethics clearance once the proposal defense is passed. entries.match: Panel matching produces a ranked shortlist of faculty for a student's defense panel
entries.replace: Panel matching produces a ranked shortlist of faculty for a student's defense panel by comparing the student's current paper with each faculty member's recorded expertise. Each candidate shows a score out of 100 built from expertise match, availability and workload, the topics and passage of the paper that matched, the expertise records used, and warning flags. A suggested panel is preselected by role, and a checklist shows whether it satisfies the composition rules of the Research Protocol. The student's adviser and co-adviser are listed as not eligible. The recommendation is advisory until the Research Coordinator or Graduate School staff finalize the panel.
entries.note: 5.10.10. PanelMatchingForm in WorkflowPage.jsx; PANEL_NOMINATION_ROLES.

entries.match: Defense scheduling proposes slots at which the student and every panel member
entries.replace: Defense scheduling proposes slots in which the research adviser and every panel member who has entered availability are simultaneously free, drawing on each person's weekly hours and dated entries and on the busy periods of a connected Google Calendar. Proposals begin only after the required lead time. Members who have not entered availability are named, and staff can ask them to enter it from the same screen. When no overlap exists the screen shows no slot for that window. A chosen slot is checked live: conflicts that cannot be saved are listed in red (a panel, venue or student overlap, a person outside the entered hours, a declined invitation, or a time in the past), and warnings that need a recorded reason are listed in amber (before the lead time, or availability not entered). Bookings can be rescheduled or cancelled, each with a recorded reason and the name of who asked, and a booking held after a panel change can be re-confirmed; the history of earlier bookings is kept. The panel invitations of each booking are shown beside it.
entries.note: 5.10.11 (rewritten after the calendar packet). defense_schedule_check (/api/defense-schedules/check), AvailabilityRequestPanel.jsx, panel invitation chips in WorkflowPage.jsx.

entries.match: The practicum screen is restricted to the programs that require a practicum.
entries.replace: The practicum screen is restricted to Psychology and MSGC students who meet the practicum eligibility checks. It shows the memorandum of agreement status, the practicum site and supervisor, the completed hours entered by the student against the required hours, and the certificate submissions, which are counted automatically and accumulate across submissions. A shortfall in hours appears as Hours Incomplete and prompts the Academic Coordinator to request additional certificates. The screen also carries the timeline through to the status report to the Dean.

entries.match: The graduation screen lists candidates for a review window
entries.replace: The graduation screen lists eligible candidates, and candidates already placed in a batch, for a review window (a school year). Each candidate's check is resolved into coursework, research and practicum, and the missing items are named for candidates returned as not eligible. Candidates are processed in named batches on a staged board: the Academic Coordinator checks coursework, the Research Coordinator validates research and practicum, staff prepare the list, and the Dean approves it or returns it for revision. After approval the Dean exports the endorsed list as a file.
entries.note: 5.10.13. StageBoard graduation (WorkflowPage.jsx), DeanGraduationPage.jsx.

entries.match: The leave of absence screen presents structured applications
entries.replace: The leave of absence screen presents each request as a card on a staged board, with a table view as an alternative. The columns are Submitted, In staff review, Returned to student, With the Dean, Leave scheduled, On leave, Return due, Ended, and Not approved. A card moves by drag and drop or by a Move to menu, and the server refuses any move the rules do not allow. The card shows the rule checks for the permitted reasons, the allowed duration (up to two semesters a request and four in total, with no limit on the number of leaves), and the filing date (no leave in the last two weeks of a semester). Staff review precedes the Dean's decision, which may be an approval, a return for revision or a denial, and a pending request may be withdrawn by the student. Selected cases can be forwarded or decided as a batch. A follow-up strip lists leaves that are ending or that ended with no return, where AWOL is proposed and staff confirm it. A Registrar list panel exports the Dean-approved cases as CSV or Excel and records when the list was sent and acknowledged; the portal sends nothing itself.
entries.note: 5.10.14. LeaveCasesBoard.jsx, leave_workflow.py BOARD_COLUMNS, FollowUpStrip.jsx, RegistrarPanel.jsx.

entries.match: Readmission follows the same structured pattern as leave of absence.
entries.replace: Readmission uses the same board and case record as leave of absence, with the columns Submitted, In staff review, Returned to student, With the Dean, Approved (back in the program), and Not approved. Staff verify the return checklist item by item before forwarding, and every request is decided by the Dean rather than resolved automatically. On approval the student is active again, the linked leave is closed, enrollment planning passes to the Academic Coordinator as a separate step, and the approved case joins the Registrar list.
entries.note: 5.10.15. leave_workflow.py readmission statuses.

entries.match: This screen combines the monitoring of students absent without leave
entries.replace: This screen combines the monitoring of students absent without leave with residency tracking. AWOL is created by the policy engine from explicit evidence and cannot be declared by hand; the engine raises an alert and a task for the Academic Coordinator, and for a leave that ended with no return AWOL is only proposed and staff confirm it. A return from AWOL is policy-reviewed and decided by the Dean, and a student beyond the absolute maximum residence requires re-enrollment rather than a simple return. Residency is derived from the recorded entry year rather than counted by hand.

entries.replace: Adviser appointment follows the protocol. The student nominates a faculty member on Form 3, which is allowed only while the student has no active adviser and no open application. The Academic Coordinator notes the application, the Research Coordinator or staff forward it to the Dean, and the Dean appoints the adviser (Form 3.1) or returns the application with a reason, after which the student may nominate again. A faculty member may hold at most five active advisees, and only the Dean, with a recorded exception and note, can exceed the limit. The nominated adviser then accepts or declines, a decline needing a reason. The student sends Forms 3.2 and 3.3 within five days of Form 3.1 (the forms travel by e-mail, so the student records that they were sent) and the Research Coordinator confirms receipt; an overdue contract is shown as a deadline. A student may change adviser once, before the proposal defense, with a reason on Form 3.1.1 that both the current and the new adviser must agree to, followed by the same Dean step; the earlier appointment then ends. An adviser appointed outside the portal can be recorded by staff or the Research Coordinator. Missing credentials, such as no recorded doctorate for a doctoral student, appear as warnings and do not block the appointment.

entries.match: Finds a defense slot at which the research adviser
entries.replace: Every role has a calendar fed by one interface: a student sees only the student's own defenses and deadlines, a faculty member sees the defenses sat on or advised, the advisees' deadlines and the member's own entered availability, and staff, the coordinators and the Dean see all defenses, the Dean's view being read-only. When a defense is booked, each panel member receives an invitation that can be accepted or declined, a decline needing a reason; a decline opens a replacement task for the Research Coordinator and blocks the booking until the seat is filled, and an adviser or panel member who cannot attend a booked defense tells the coordinators, who must reschedule. Notifications are in-app only, and no e-mail is sent: a bell in the top bar shows read and unread items with their links and due dates, for adviser steps, invitations, availability requests, and defenses booked, moved or cancelled, and reminders for a defense are created when the bell is opened, 14, 7, 2 and 1 days before it. Each person can create a private calendar link (an .ics feed whose secret address is the credential, replaceable and revocable at any time), and each booked defense can be downloaded as a single calendar event.
